text:
I found no study establishing the exact frozen-SASRec mixture comparison requested. Closest: [Do Sequential Recommendation Benchmarks Require Higher-Order Sequence Modelling?](https://research.atspotify.com/2026/10/do-sequential-recommendation-benchmarks-require-higher-order-sequence-modelling) compares SASRec/eSASRec against last-item Markov models and recency-weighted pairwise history models, with separately tunable popularity adjustment. Pairwise models outperform both Transformer reproductions on four of five benchmarks; this supports testing simple temporal controls, but does not establish benefits from mixing frozen SASRec embeddings. [NISER](https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.04276) directly connects popularity bias to representation norms and studies normalization, although in session-based graph recommendation rather than frozen SASRec.

Recommended matched ablation: freeze one SASRec checkpoint; compare its scores alone and mixtures with last-item similarity, recent-k embedding means, full-history means, and training-frequency popularity. Give every mixture identical validation tuning and score calibration. Cross raw dot products with unit-normalized item embeddings/cosine; normalize history embeddings before averaging as a separate control. Dot products can favor large-norm, frequent items, as explained in [Google’s similarity comparison](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/recommendation/overview/candidate-generation). Compare recent-k against equally sized random and oldest-k subsets; permuting history alone cannot change an unweighted mean. Include candidate-norm-only and popularity-only additions to isolate generic score effects.

For durable goods, treat “recent purchase satisfied the need” as a hypothesis, not an observed user trait. [Buy It Again](https://www.amazon.science/publications/buy-it-again-modeling-repeat-purchase-recommendations) studies repeat-purchase timing, not proof that similar unseen products should be suppressed. Test positive versus negative similarity weights and timestamp-dependent effects using available histories; report category results alongside macro validation HR@10 under the unchanged evaluator.
